item.title: Void Rift
item.description:
The Void Rift is an advanced time-manipulation building that provides powerful, permanent boosts to both your storage capacity and energy production in the late game.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite: To unlock the Void Rift, you must first acquire the Void Aspiration upgrade.
  • Cost: The first Void Rift requires an investment of 75 Void.
  • Price Ratio: The cost scales with a 1.3 price ratio for each subsequent purchase.

Core Effects

  • Global Storage Boost: Each Void Rift permanently increases all of your global resource storage capacity by 2%. This specific storage bonus stacks additively with the 10% storage bonus provided by Event Horizons, and scales multiplicatively alongside other storage bonuses like those from Paragon.
  • Energy Production: Each Void Rift also increases the energy production of your HR Harvesters by 10%. Because HR Harvesters scale infinitely with Dark Future years, accumulating Void Rifts is an excellent way to drastically multiply your late-game power output.

Endgame Strategy

In the deep endgame, acquiring dozens of Void Rifts becomes a primary objective to accelerate your resource velocity. A common strategic milestone is to amass around 200 million Void to purchase 50 Void Rifts.

A Data Centre is a high-tier scientific building that serves as the direct upgrade to the Library. It provides significantly enhanced storage for science and culture, and it is a critical component for reaching the massive science caps required for late-game progression.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Unlocking: You must research Electronics (135k Science, 70 Blueprints) to enable the option to upgrade Libraries into Data Centres.
  • Cost: Each Data Centre costs 10 Concrete and 100 Steel.
  • Energy Requirement: Unlike Libraries, which are energy-neutral, each Data Centre consumes 2 Watts of energy.

Primary Effects and Benefits

Once a Library is upgraded, the resulting Data Centre provides the following bonuses:

  • Science Production: Grants a +10% bonus to overall science production.
  • Science Storage: Increases the maximum science cap by 750.
  • Culture Storage: Increases the maximum culture cap by 250.
  • Compendium Efficiency: Provides a +1,000 increase to the Compendium Cap, allowing you to store more science via crafted compendiums.

Workshop Upgrades and Synergies

Data Centres can be made exponentially more powerful through specific Workshop research:

  • Cryocomputing: This upgrade (from Superconductors) reduces energy consumption by 50%, bringing the drain down from 2 Watts to 1 Watt per building.
  • Uplink: Creates a synergy with Bio Labs, increasing the science and culture caps of Data Centres by +1% per Bio Lab owned.
  • Reflectors (Titanium, Unobtainium, and Eludium): These upgrades allow your Observatories to boost the effectiveness of Data Centres. Each built Observatory provides an additive +2% bonus to the Data Centre’s science capacity.
  • Machine Learning: This Artificial Intelligence upgrade increases the effectiveness of Data Centres by +10% for every AI Core built.
  • Starlink: Further enhances the Uplink synergy by providing additional bonuses to science caps.

Strategic Utility

  • Efficiency Scaling: One Data Centre provides the same maximum science as three Libraries. This makes them highly space-efficient for players struggling to hit the science requirements for advanced technologies like Chronophysics.
  • The “Dead Stop” Warning: You should never upgrade your last Library if you do not have the materials (Concrete and Steel) to immediately build a Data Centre. If you have zero Libraries and zero Data Centres, astronomical events will cease to occur, halting your supply of starcharts.
  • Blueprint Crafting: Be aware that switching to Data Centres may initially decrease your bonus for crafting blueprints if you end up with fewer total buildings than you had as Libraries. This can be mitigated through the CAD System upgrade, which applies a +1% craft ratio per scientific building.
  • Energy Management: Because they consume energy, mass-upgrading Libraries into Data Centres can quickly crash your power grid. It is often wise to wait until your energy production (via Magnetos or Reactors) is stable before performing a bulk upgrade.

The Unicorn Pasture is an early gateway into the complex Unicorn/Religion Era of the game:

  • Early Hunting Goal: The walkthrough advises that if you are lucky, hunting will yield unicorns, and once you “Find two Unicorns, you can create a Unicorn Pasture”.

  • Foundation for Unicorn Era: Unicorn Pastures are the starting point for the entire unicorn resource production line, which eventually leads to Tears, Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS), Alicorns, and Time Crystals.
  • Upgrades: Unicorn Pasture generation can be boosted by the Unicorn Selection workshop upgrade, which increases production by +25%.

Once the Unicorn Pasture is established, you can proceed with the religious path that utilizes Unicorns and Tears:

  • Ziggurats: Unicorns are required to build Ziggurats (unlocked by Construction). Ziggurats enable you to Sacrifice Unicorns (2500 Unicorns per sacrifice) to receive Unicorn Tears.
  • Tears Consumption: Tears are then used to purchase advanced Unicorn buildings that further boost unicorn generation, such as Unicorn Tomb, Ivory Tower, Ivory Citadel, Sky Palace, Unicorn Utopia, and Sunspire. These buildings are the key to the Unicorn/Time Crystal Era.

In essence, the Unicorn Pasture takes a rare, sporadic hunting bonus (the Unicorn) and turns it into a reliable, automated luxury resource, while simultaneously providing a permanent reduction in the cost of kitten maintenance.

  • Early Game Priority: Unlocking Agriculture and then purchasing Barns is essential to quickly establish a strong economic foundation. They are classified as general storage buildings that should be built “as needed”.

Barns benefit from several workshop upgrades, many of which apply across multiple storage structures (Barns, Warehouses, and Harbors):

  • Direct Capacity Increases:
    • Expanded Barns: Increases max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 75%.
    • Reinforced Barns: Increases max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 80%.
    • Titanium Barns and Alloy Barns: Each increase max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 100%.
    • Concrete Barns: Increases max storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron by 75%.
  • General Storage Upgrades: Barns also benefit from upgrades that apply broadly to common resource storage across multiple buildings, such as Reinforced Warehouses, Titanium Warehouses, Alloy Warehouses, and Concrete Warehouses.
  • Concrete Pillars: This upgrade increases the maximum storage for Wood, Minerals, and Iron from Barns and Warehouses by 5%. It also applies a 5% bonus to max Coal, Gold, and Titanium storage from Barns and other facilities.
  • Silos Synergy: Although Warehouses are the only building that can directly store Catnip via the Silos upgrade, once Silos is researched, all storage upgrades with “barns” in their name apply 25% of their effect to maximum Catnip storage as well.

The Calciner is an industrial building in Kittens Game that plays a key role in mid-to-late game resource refinement, specifically concerning Iron and Titanium production.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Calciner’s purpose, costs, effects, and strategic importance, drawing on the sources:

1. Construction and Unlocks

  • Prerequisite Technology: The Calciner building is unlocked by researching the Chemistry technology. Chemistry is a late-Physics technology.

The Calciner’s primary function is advanced refinement, specifically converting minerals and oil into Iron and Titanium:

    • It consumes 1.5 Minerals per tick.
    • It consumes 0.024 Oil per tick.
  • Output Production (Conversion Production):
    • It produces 0.15 Iron per tick.
    • It produces 0.0005 Titanium per tick.

Calciners are one of the core buildings whose production counts as “Conversion production”.

3. Upgrades and Enhancements

The efficiency of Calciners can be significantly boosted through Workshop upgrades, usually unlocked by Metallurgy and Nanotechnology:

Upgrade Name Effect Prerequisite
Oxidation Increases Iron production by +95% and Titanium production by +285%. Metallurgy.
Rotary Kiln Increases Iron production by +75% and Titanium production by +225%. Robotics.
Fluidized Reactors Increases Iron production by +100% and Titanium production by +300%. Nanotechnology.
Steel Plants Converts 10% of the Calciner’s Iron output into Steel (100:1 ratio), decreasing the final Iron output by 10%. Robotics.
Automated Plants Boosts the Steel production from Steel Plants by 25% of the general craft ratio. Steel Plants.
Nuclear Plants Boosts the Steel production from Steel Plants by an additional 2% per active Reactor. Automated Plants.
Policy Bonus The Autocracy policy provides a bonus of 0.4% per leader rank per uncapped population building to all conversion production, which includes Calciners.
Policy Bonus The Griffin Relations: Metallurgists policy increases the Calciner’s steel production bonus by +15%. Griffin Embassy Level 20, Diplomacy metaphysics.

4. Strategic Role and Recommendations

Calciners are a type of building that boosts general production but costs hard-to-acquire blueprints.

  • Resource Focus: They are one of the main ways to produce Iron and Titanium.

  • Energy Consumption: Each Factory consumes -2 Energy.
  • Pollution: Factories are listed among the structures that produce pollution. However, pollution produced by factories can be reduced to zero by the Carbon Sequestration upgrade.

3. Upgrades and Policy Interactions

Factories are central to several mid-to-late-game scaling mechanics:

  • Policy Prerequisite: Factories are required to unlock high-tier Government Policy/ such as Liberalism, Communism, and Fascism.
    • If you choose the Full Industrialization policy (which follows Strip Mining or Clear Cutting), the crafting bonus from Factories is further improved by 5% (e.g., from +5% to +5.25%, or from +6% to +6.3% depending on upgrades). This policy is recommended from the second run onward, as players will be building many Factories.
  • Crafting Boost Upgrades:
    • The Factory Logistics Workshop upgrade increases the craft bonus of Factories by an additional +1%.
  • Space Manufacturing: The Space Manufacturing upgrade enables Factories to improve Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays by 3.75% per factory (4.5% with Factory Logistics). This bonus is crucial because most production bonuses (like Paragon and Magnetos) do not apply to space structures, making Factories one of the few ways to increase space building production efficiency.
  • Oil and Refinement: The Factory Processing upgrade, unlocked by Oil Processing Science, causes every Factory to increase oil refinement effectiveness by 5%. Factories also help oil production once the Hydraulic Fracturers are employed (unlocked by the Dune Mission).
  • Pollution Mitigation: The Carbon Sequestration upgrade allows Factories to capture pollution from the atmosphere instead of creating it by consuming 4Wt of energy per Factory, reducing pollution by 2 points per tick.

4. Strategic Role

Factories are built to enhance the creation of complex resources needed for endgame technologies, especially in subsequent runs.

  • Endgame Crafting: Factories are maximized (along with Workshops) to increase the crafting ratio, which helps reduce the number of crafts needed to produce high-tier materials like Eludium.
  • Unobtainium Production: Factories are instrumental in maximizing Unobtainium production in the late game through the Space Manufacturing upgrade. They contribute to the space production bonus via the number of Factories and the Factory Logistics upgrade.
  • Blueprint Generation: Factories contribute indirectly to the essential task of generating Blueprints by boosting the crafting process (Furs $\to$ Parchment $\to$ Manuscript $\to$ Compendium $\to$ Blueprint).
  • Building Priority: Factories are one of the key production-boosting structures that “should be built provided you have the resources to use on them” in the mid-to-late game.

Oil Wells are critical, as Oil quickly becomes a bottleneck resource during the transition to space exploration.

Upgrade Name Effect Prerequisite

This automation is necessary for overcoming the steep requirements of the later Theology and Astronomy sciences.

  2. Resource Conversion: The Workshop Automation upgrade allows Steamworks to automatically convert a percentage of wood into beams and minerals into slabs once per year when those resources are nearly capped (at 98% of capacity).   3. Industrial Foundation: Steamworks are listed among the supplemental production-boosting buildings (alongside Magnetos, Reactors, Calciners, and Quarrys) that cost blueprints and help create base resources.

Upgrades and Efficiency

Several upgrades directly affect the Steamworks’ efficiency and resource consumption:

  • Coal Efficiency: The High Pressure Engine and Fuel Injector upgrades each reduce the Coal consumption of Steamworks by 20%.
  • Magneto Synergy: The Magneto Boost is further improved by the Griffin Relations: Machinists policy, which increases the Steamworks’ Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.

Contextual Notes

  • Prerequisite Grinding: The Steamworks presents a hurdle because it requires Blueprints and Gears (which require Steel). In the IW 40K run, the Sharks and Griffins trading loop is cited as a key method for collecting the necessary steel, gears, and blueprints for Steamworks.
  • Coal Management: Since Steamworks consume coal, players are advised to turn off Steamworks when grinding coal for other priorities, such as building Oil Wells.
  • Challenges:
    • The Steamworks is listed as a necessary building to complete the Energy Challenge.
    • In the Pacifism Challenge, the cost of the Steamworks increases by 1.5, rounded down to the nearest integer, and the blueprint cost linearly increases by 5.

The Magneto building receives a direct, inherent boost from the Steamworks.

  • Magneto Boost: Each Steamworks provides a +15% Magneto Boost. This increases the Magneto’s effect of providing a +2% Global Production bonus.
  • Policy Enhancement: This Magneto boost provided by the Steamworks can be further improved by the Griffin Relations: Machinists policy, which increases the Steamwork’s Magneto boost bonus by +0.5%.

5. Manuscripts (Automated Production)

The Steamworks facility can be upgraded to automate the production of the advanced resource Manuscripts.

  • Printing Press: The Printing Press upgrade allows Steamworks to produce Manuscript per Tick +0.0005 (or 0.0025 manuscripts/sec). This requires the Steamworks building (unlocked by Machinery).
  • Further Upgrades: This automated production rate can be substantially increased by subsequent Workshop upgrades:
    • Offset Press increases manuscript production by a factor of 4 (to 0.01 manuscripts/sec).
    • Photolithography also increases manuscript production by a factor of 4 (to 0.04 manuscripts/sec).

3. Crafted Resources (Automation)

The core functionality of the Workshop benefits from Steamworks through automated material conversion:

  • Workshop Automation: Steamworks unlock the Workshop Automation upgrade, which causes the Steamworks to convert resources into craftable materials when those resources reach their cap.
    • Once per year, Steamworks convert wood (to beams) and minerals (to slabs) at $98%$ of the resource’s cap.
    • The Advanced Automation upgrade allows this conversion to activate twice per year.
  • Pneumatic Press: This upgrade further expands the automation to include iron being converted to plates.

Strategic Considerations

It is noted that Steamworks consume coal. In the mid-game, experts advise against keeping Steamworks active unless you plan to be idle for long periods, as running them can severely restrict your coal production.

2. Primary Functions of the Workshop Tab

The Workshop tab contains three main sections:

A. Upgrades

This section allows players to purchase upgrades that are essential for improving overall village productivity, resource efficiency, and kitten functionality.

  • Purpose: Upgrades generally improve the efficiency of buildings or workers, which is highly beneficial in the long run.
  • Examples: Upgrades unlocked here include Reinforced Saw (Lumber Mill efficiency), Gold Ore (Smelters produce gold), Composite Bow (Hunter catpower boost), and Caravanserai (Trade relations boost).

B. Crafting

This section allows for the creation of composite materials necessary for advanced buildings and subsequent technological progression.

  • Purpose: Crafted items are generally composite parts for buildings, and advanced structures require a fair amount of crafting to complete.
  • Craftable Resources: The Workshop is used to convert basic resources into crucial craftable resources like Beam, Slab, Plate, Steel, and later, Manuscript, Compendium, and Blueprint.
  • Exchange: The Workshop also allows you to exchange Catnip directly for basic resources.
  • Automation: The Engineer job, enabled by Mechanization technology, allows kittens to automate crafting within the Workshop.

C. Zebra Upgrades

This section houses upgrades that become available once the Zebra Workshop building is constructed.

The decision to build Amphitheatres is a major early-game strategic step, as it addresses a key bottleneck in the technology tree:

  • Culture Grind: Amphitheatres are one of the earliest buildings to generate Culture. This resource requirement creates a significant hurdle, forcing players to focus on culture generation.
  • Managing Population Happiness: As your kitten population grows (by building Huts and Log Houses, which you should keep maxed out), they become unhappy. Since Happiness dictates the overall efficiency of your Kittens in their work, Amphitheatres are extremely important in the early game to reduce unhappiness and maintain high production levels.
    • It is advised to build Amphitheatres until they stop noticeably improving Happiness, which can be monitored via the ‘population penalty’ percentage on the top bar of the game.
  • Preparation for Temples: Amphitheatres help make obtaining Temples easier, as Temples are another structure that generates Culture.
  • Building Priority: When happiness starts becoming a serious problem, players should consider pushing for the Writing science to unlock Amphitheatres. You may need to temporarily employ all kittens as Hunters to stockpile the Parchment required to craft them.

Upgrades and Progression

  • Upgrade Path: The Amphitheatre can be upgraded to a Broadcast Tower. This upgrade is unlocked by researching Electronics.
  • Broadcast Tower Conversion: The Broadcast Tower upgrade offers a significant boost to culture production and unhappiness reduction, with a single tower potentially replacing an entire stock of Amphitheatres for happiness purposes. A single tower increases the culture cap as much as six Amphitheatres, and increases culture production as much as “two hundred”. There is generally little reason to delay this upgrade once the metal is available to build a tower.

  • AI Apocalypse Risk: Accumulating Gigaflops can potentially lead to the AI Apocalypse. If the AI level reaches 15, you start losing resources.
  • Synergy with Entanglement Stations: AI Cores are typically built alongside Entanglement Stations (unlocked by Quantum Cryptography), which produce Hashes. The combination of AI Cores and Entanglement Stations creates hashes, which increase the hashrate level.
  • Ratio Management: When building AI Cores and Entanglement Stations, players must monitor the Gigaflops accumulation to avoid the AI Apocalypse. The ratio is suggested to be roughly 5 AI Cores to 1 Entanglement Station to prevent excessive Gigaflops accumulation, especially since Gigaflops are always lost on reset.

3. Upgrades and Policy Synergies

The effectiveness of AI Cores can be enhanced through specific Workshop upgrades and Government Policy/:

  • Machine Learning: This Workshop upgrade makes Data Center effectiveness increase by +10% per AI Core. The effect is based on the number of AI Cores built, not the AI level.
  • AI Bases: This Workshop upgrade increases Moon Base storage by +10% per AI Core. The effect is also based on the number of AI Cores.
  • Transkittenism Policy: This late-game government policy makes AI Cores twice as effective. The AI Cores produce twice as many Gigaflops, and the policy ensures that the AI apocalypse will not occur. Furthermore, AI Bases and the Machine Learning upgrades are strengthened.
  • Anarchy Challenge Goal: Interestingly, the AI Core is specified as the building that must be built to complete the Anarchy challenge.

Strategic Importance

Building Catnip Fields is the first step in establishing a stable food supply, which is critical because every kitten consumes Catnip:

  • Initial Progression: Purchasing fields allows Catnip to accumulate on its own without requiring further manual clicking. Buying multiple fields early (up to 19 or 20) is advised to speed up progress.
  • Basic Resource Rotation (BRR): The earliest routine for building a strong economic foundation involves taking all kittens and making them farmers, and then capping (or close to capping) everything that ONLY costs catnip, which includes Catnip Fields.
  • Diminishing Returns: Eventually, the fields become too expensive and do not produce enough to be truly useful. At this stage, players are advised to research Engineering and build Aqueducts instead, which increase Catnip production by a percentile.
  • Storage: The default maximum storage capacity for Catnip is 5000.

Seasonal and Environmental Effects

Catnip Fields are highly susceptible to the game’s weather system, especially during the harsh Winter season:

  • Seasonal Fluctuations: Production values change radically throughout the year.
    • In Spring, production receives a hefty bonus (average +50%).
    • In Winter, production sharply nosedives (average -75%).
    • A Cold Winter can reduce Catnip production by -90%.
  • Contrast with Farmers: Unlike the Catnip accumulated by the Farmer job (which produces +1 Catnip per tick), the production from Catnip Fields is subject to the effects of Winter. Juggling Catnip production is crucial for survival, particularly in Winter.

Challenge and Policy Interactions

Catnip Fields are affected by specific late-game Policy/ and challenges:

  • Communism Policy: This policy causes Catnip Field production to become -100% in cold winters.
  • Winter Has Come Challenge: When this challenge (which imposes endless winter) is active, Catnip production from fields will not benefit from the paragon production bonus. The increasing reward for completing this challenge increases the effect of Spring on Catnip Fields by 5% per run.
  • Post Apocalypse Challenge: In this high-pollution scenario, Catnip Fields may cost unobtainium at high pollution levels or with high numbers of broken cryochambers.

In the early game, managing Catnip production from these fields is like stocking a simple pantry: you have to gather enough food during the bounty of spring and summer to ensure you have reserves large enough to survive the consumption during winter’s famine.

Upgrading Aqueducts to Hydro Plants represents a crucial transition from basic resource augmentation to industrial power generation. This decision carries significant risk:

  • Automation: The increase in Automatic Event Observation Chance is crucial because it reduces the player’s need to manually click the “Observe” button whenever an astronomical event occurs. Strategic Context

The Bio Lab is strategically important but carries a heavy upfront cost:

  • Science Scaling: Bio Labs are listed as buildings that increase science cap, helping players reach high science limits needed for advanced technology.
  • Late-Game Utility: To reach the 125K science limit required for Concrete Huts, players are advised to consider researching Biology to unlock Bio Labs, as they increase science and help “reduce the need to build so many observatories/temples (which start getting very costly)”.
  • Expense: However, Bio Labs are noted to be “really expensive on your first couple runs,” and new players may want to “feel free to skip it first time around”. In later runs, they may still be skipped if high Paragon levels already provide a sufficient storage boost.
  • Pollution: Bio Labs are one of the many industrial buildings that produce Pollution.

Key Upgrades and Synergies

The Bio Lab’s function shifts significantly through specific upgrades, allowing it to become an oil production facility and synergizing with other science structures:

A. Oil Conversion Upgrades

The following upgrades allow the Bio Lab to convert food resources into Oil, requiring energy:

  1. Biofuel Processing (Unlocked by Biochemistry): This upgrade causes Bio Labs to consume 5 Catnip per second (or 1 Catnip per tick) and consume 1 Energy per tick. In return, it produces 0.10 Oil per second (or 0.02 Oil per tick). Additionally, it grants a +35% Science bonus.
  2. GM Catnip (Unlocked by Genetics): This upgrade improves the Bio Lab’s oil yield by +60% (multiplicative with other effects), although it does not affect the amount of Catnip consumed.
  3. Shark Relations: Botanists Policy: This foreign policy reduces the Bio Lab’s energy consumption by 75%.

B. Science and Data Center Synergy

Bio Labs interact closely with the late-game Data Center building, which is an upgrade to the Library:

  1. Uplink (Unlocked by Satellites): This upgrade creates a reciprocal bonus: Data Centers gain a +1% bonus to Max Science, Max Culture, and Compendium Cap per Bio Lab, and Bio Labs gain a +1% Max Science bonus per Data Center.
  2. Starlink (Unlocked by Orbital Engineering): Further increases the Max Science bonus of Bio Labs by +1% per Data Center.
  3. CAD System (Unlocked by Electronics): Bio Labs are one of the specific scientific buildings (along with Libraries/Data Centers, Academies, and Observatories) that improve the effectiveness of Blueprint crafting via the CAD System workshop upgrade. Bio Labs contribute this bonus even when they are turned off.

The Bio Lab thus facilitates the transition into the oil and advanced science era, often being built primarily for its energy-efficient method of converting excess catnip into valuable oil resources.

2. Strategic Role and Bottleneck Mitigation

Accelerators help address the significant bottleneck of obtaining Uranium, which is required for Reactors and later converted into Unobtainium by the Lunar Outpost.

  • Uranium Source: It is one of the ways Uranium can be produced, alongside trading with Dragons and production from Quarries after the Orbital Geodesy upgrade.
  • Efficiency Concerns: The initial conversion rate is slow; one Accelerator creates Uranium at a rate 140 times slower than a Lunar Outpost consumes it. This means if the Accelerator is the sole source of Uranium, the Lunar Outpost will run 140 times slower. Players are advised to create multiple Accelerators to speed things up, or rely on trading with Dragons for Uranium.
  • Dark Future Mitigation: Accelerators can be purchased to “ward off” the rising Time Crystal cost caused by the “dark future” mechanic, although players are advised not to worry about this too much as the effect is minimal.

3. Key Upgrades (Energy Rifts)

The most notable feature of the Accelerator is its ability to unlock substantial storage upgrades through the “Energy Rifts” technology, significantly boosting resource capacity.

Upgrade Name Technology Prerequisite Effect (Storage Boost per Accelerator)
Energy Rifts Dimensional Physics Unlocks substantial storage capacity for Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Iron, Coal, Gold, and Titanium.
Stasis Chambers Chronophysics Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +95%.
Void Energy Stasis Chambers Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +75%.
Dark Energy Void Energy Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +250%.
Tachyon Accelerators Tachyon Theory Increases the storage gain from Energy Rifts by +500%.

Furthermore, the LHC upgrade (unlocked by Dimensional Physics) provides a bonus of +2500 Max Science per Accelerator.

In the late game, using the Energy Rift upgrade is key to increasing storage capacity for unobtainium.

4. Challenge Context

  • Energy Challenge: The Accelerator is not listed among the necessary buildings required to complete the Energy Challenge, which focuses on energy production buildings (Steamworks, Magneto, Solar Farms, Hydro Plant, Reactor, Satellite, Sunlifter, Tectonic, HR Harvester).
  • Paragon Grind: In the Paragon grinding phase, after the 40K mark, the advice is to buy a few Time Impedances and Accelerators to slow down the rising Time Crystal cost due to “dark future”.

The Amphitheatre building is unlocked once you research the Writing technology.

  • Base Cost: 2,500 Unobtainium, 1 Time Crystal, 100 Blueprint, and 250,000 Science.
  • Price Ratio: 1.25.

2. Core Functions and Effects

The Chronosphere has several critical, interrelated functions that affect resource management and game mechanics:

  • Resource Preservation on Reset: Its main purpose is to preserve a percentage of your non-crafted, non-luxury resources upon resetting the game. Each Chronosphere preserves 1.5% of these resources (Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Oil, Uranium, etc.).
    • If the total preservation percentage exceeds 100%, you receive multiple units of those resources upon reset.
  • Void Generation: Chronospheres are necessary for generating Void. Void is a unique resource that is generated randomly every year change if you have Chronospheres.
  • Energy Consumption: It consumes -20 Energy per tick to operate.
  • Temporal Flux Generation (Upgrade): While the base function generates Temporal Flux at a rate of 5 units per minute when the game is not active, the Chronosurge upgrade causes each Chronosphere to generate 1 flux per year.
  • Temporal Paradox: It has an associated risk: “Occasional Temporal Paradox”.

3. Strategic Importance and Progression

The Chronosphere is strategically vital for transitioning into high-paragon, high-speed runs and the late-game resource cycles:

  • Accelerating Future Runs (The Seed): By building multiple Chronospheres, players can carry over essential late-game resources (like unobtanium, antimatter, and blueprints). This drastically speeds up subsequent runs, allowing players to immediately purchase most high-tier technologies and upgrades after a reset.
  • The Chrono-Reset Loop: The concept of the “quick” chrono-reset involves building Chronospheres out of the resource profit generated from the reset itself, leading to faster paragon farming.
  • Void Acquisition: The Void resource generated by Chronospheres is needed to unlock high-tier Metaphysics upgrades (like Void Space and Paradox Theory) and to purchase upgrades like Cryochambers and Void Rifts.
  • Unobtainium Capacity Goal: A late-game goal is to build enough Chronospheres to reach an extreme Unobtainium capacity (e.g., 8.14 billion UO capacity to build 100 Chronospheres).

4. Key Upgrades (Flux Condensator)

The utility of the Chronosphere is greatly enhanced by the Flux Condensator upgrade:

  • Flux Condensator: This upgrade costs 250 Alloy, 5,000 Unobtainium, and 5 Time Crystals.
    • It causes Chronospheres to affect craftable resources (like Beam, Slab, Steel, Blueprint, and Megalith).
    • The amount preserved is calculated with diminishing returns: $1.5 ({# of Chronospheres}) \sqrt{{resource amount}}$** of each craftable resource is carried over on reset.

5. Challenge Interaction

  • Challenges and Reserves: When resetting with most challenges active, Chronospheres will not bring over any resources. Instead, resources are placed in reserves and can be reclaimed after the challenge is complete.
  • Iron Will: Iron Will mode is entered by resetting with zero Chronospheres.

The Ziggurat’s most important function is enabling the conversion of Unicorns into Unicorn Tears.

  • Sacrifice Unicorns: Once you have a Ziggurat, you unlock the ability to Sacrifice Unicorns in the Religion tab.
  • Cost and Yield: Each sacrifice costs 2500 Unicorns. In return, you receive one Unicorn Tear for every Ziggurat you have.
  • Initial Benefit: The resulting Unicorn Tear provides a happiness/production bonus.

3. Strategic Importance

The Ziggurat is the entry point to the “Unicorn/Time Crystal Era”.

  • Culture Boost: The Ziggurat provides a passive effect of Max Culture +8%.
  • Resource Pipeline: The Ziggurat establishes the beginning of a crucial late-game resource line: unicorns → tears → Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) → alicorns → time crystals → relics.
  • Building Priority (Early Game): Expert advice suggests that if a player needs to ask if they should get Ziggurats, they “probably don’t need more than one” on their first few runs, due to the expensive nature of the entire resource line. It is advised to build one Ziggurat when possible, sacrificing unicorns for one tear for the initial bonus, as you “won’t need more than one tear until you hit the unicorn era”.
  • Building Priority (Late Game): In the Unicorn Era, players are advised to build a large number of ziggurats. For the IW 40K endless run, it is suggested to build at least 10 Ziggurats before converting unicorns, with 25–30 Ziggurats being the practical maximum due to resource costs.

4. Upgrades and Synergies

The Ziggurat interacts with other buildings and Policy/:

  • Religious Synergy (Nagas): The Naga Relations: Cultists policy (a Foreign policy) allows Ziggurats to gain 10% of the bonuses The Order of the Sun grants to temples.
  • Culture Capacity (Unicorn Graveyard): The Unicorn Graveyard building (unlocked by Megalomania/Black Codex) increases your culture maximum by +1% per Ziggurat.
  • Unicorn Rift Bonus: The amount of unicorns gained from a Unicorn Rift (a random event unlocked by Ivory Towers) is boosted, calculated as 500 * (1 + your unicorn ziggurat bonus production to unicorns/10).
